harness.name: final-kernel-baseline-full-prewarm-workers1
limits: Collector delivery adds latency to observation; app elapsed and host monotonic origins differ.
One fresh process; SQLite may already be running.
Application elapsed_ms starts at its first timing call; host mono_ms has a separate origin. Request identity joins records, not clocks.

Loader interval is measured entirely in host mono_ms from prebind begin to guest_entry end. guest_entry ends before invoking application entry; Hull/bootstrap work before application timing origin is not bridged.
No end-to-end total is derived by adding loader duration to an application endpoint.
Nested/concurrent host phases overlap and must not be summed. AP preparation includes its unpack/inspect/arenas/assets/files/environment child spans.
Host request IDs are unique within this boot only; kernel publication and fresh-boot evidence scope the request identity.
Request 1 identifies Codex; request 2 is the separate cold SQLite service launch. SQLite has no application-side timing row here.
Source-stamped elapsed durations and scheduler continuations are wall time, not CPU time. First-flush/readiness markers do not establish physical SSH presentation or every submission guard.
The baseline uses one explicit async worker and a cold SQLite service. It is not directly comparable to earlier two-worker or warm-service observations.
Only recognized timing/diagnostic fields and controlled-test metadata are retained; no unrelated account/chat log content is copied.
The warm-service repeat has request 3 and retains SQLite from request 2; request identity remains scoped to this single boot.

The final-kernel-baseline observation belongs to a later fresh boot and carries its own publication_receipt and fresh_boot. The root publication_receipt/fresh_boot scope only the initial cold/warm pair; request IDs may repeat across boots.

The final-kernel-baseline has cold SQLite again after returning to the original instrumented-off kernel. Its 30-second no-input window differs from the initial pair's 5-second window; compare source timing endpoints separately from readiness booleans and echo timing.
